title: BroPS Approval Request (desktop to engine)
description: An UNSIGNED, unauthenticated ask that the engine RECORDS and does not act on. It exists because Phase 2's acceptance criteria require that the owner can request an approval the ENGINE adjudicates, and because the artifact that adjudicates one already exists and must not be confused with this: `control-room-command.schema.json` carries `key_id` and a detached Ed25519 `signature` over the JCS-canonical payload, and the engine verifies it. The desktop cannot mint that, and must not appear to. So the two compose rather than overlap: the desktop asks, the engine records the ask in its own store, and an owner-signed control-room command is what decides. A reply to this document says RECORDED; there is no field in which it could say GRANTED. Five invariants are fixed here rather than by whoever implements the transport: no key, lease, nonce or verdict crosses the wall in this direction; the desktop requests and never decides; the desktop's own local approval authority (T-010/T-011 over SQLite) is a different thing with a different name; `RECORDS_ARE_AUTHENTICATED` stays false, so `requested_by` is a NAME and never an authenticated identity; and this schema is audited before the transport that carries it lands.

protocol.description: Held as a literal in both the engine and the bridge, with a test asserting the two are equal, exactly as `brops.governance-read.v1` is.

request_id.description: Generated by the caller so a retry is recognisable as the same ask. It is a correlation id and nothing else: it grants nothing, and the engine treats a repeat as a duplicate record rather than as a second decision.

requested_command.description: The control-room command the requester is ASKING an owner to issue, named with the vocabulary `control-room-command.schema.json` already uses rather than a second set of words for the same three acts. The page's `grant` / `deny` / `escalate` map onto these. `cancel`, `retry` and `reassign` are deliberately absent: they are not approvals, and a request shape wide enough to drive the whole command surface would be a command channel with a softer name.

expected_task_state.description: The state the requester believes the task is in. The engine refuses a request whose expectation does not match what it holds, so a stale cockpit cannot ask about a task that has moved on. This is the same field name, and the same purpose, as on the signed command.

evidence_refs.description: References to evidence the engine already holds. References, not contents: nothing here is a new input to the engine's trust boundary, and a ref that resolves to nothing is the engine's to refuse.

requested_by_type.description: One value, deliberately. `control-room-command` allows `owner` or `bro`, both of which the engine can authenticate; this direction can authenticate neither, so it says what it is. A request claiming to be the owner would be a claim this transport cannot support.

requested_by.description: A NAME, never an authenticated identity. `RECORDS_ARE_AUTHENTICATED` is permanently false in this repository, so the engine records this string as what was CLAIMED, beside how it was established, which is: not at all.
